questions.question: Kulhads are disposable cups made of clay. A little thought shows that making these kulhads on a large scale would result in:

__

• The top-soil is the most fertile part of the soil, containing essential nutrients for plant growth.
 
• Excessive removal of this top layer for making kulhads can lead to soil degradation and reduced agricultural productivity.
 
• Loss of fertile top-soil adversely affects crop yields, impacting food security and farmers' livelihoods.
 
• Soil erosion and desertification can be accelerated by the removal of the top-soil layer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Top-soil**

 
 
• The uppermost layer of soil, typically 5-20 cm deep, rich in organic material and microorganisms.
 
• It is crucial for plant growth, as it holds water and nutrients.
 
• Top-soil conservation is essential for sustainable agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Soil Degradation**
 
 
• The decline in soil quality caused by its improper use or poor management.
 
• It can result from erosion, loss of soil structure, and nutrient depletion.
 
• Soil degradation leads to reduced agricultural productivity and ecological imbalance.
 
 
 
• **Soil Conservation Methods**
 
 
• Practices such as crop rotation, cover cropping, and contour plowing help in preventing soil erosion.
 
• Maintaining vegetation cover and applying organic matter improve soil structure and fertility.
 
• Soil conservation is vital for long-term agricultural sustainability and environmental health.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture**
 
 
• Loss of fertile top-soil reduces the land's agricultural potential.
 
• Farmers face lower crop yields and increased costs for fertilizers and soil amendments.
 
• Sustainable soil management practices are necessary to ensure food security and rural livelihoods.

questions.question: The smallest particle of an element that retains its properties is called a/an:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**atom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An **atom** is the smallest particle of an element that retains all the chemical properties of that element.
 
• Atoms consist of a nucleus, containing protons and neutrons, surrounded by electrons.
 
• Different elements have different numbers of protons, which is the atomic number that defines the element.
 
• The structure of atoms determines the way they interact with other atoms to form compounds and molecules.
 
• Atoms are the basic building blocks of matter and can join together to form molecules, which are the substances that make up the world around us.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electron**

 
 
• Electrons are subatomic particles with a negative charge.
 
• They orbit the nucleus of an atom in various energy levels or shells.
 
• Electrons play a crucial role in chemical bonds and reactions.
 
 
 
• **Proton**
 
 
• Protons are positively charged subatomic particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of protons (atomic number) defines the element.
 
• Protons, along with neutrons, give the atom its mass.
 
 
 
• **Neutron**
 
 
• Neutrons are neutral subatomic particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• They contribute to the mass of an atom but do not affect its charge.
 
• Neutrons play a key role in the stability of an atom's nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Compound**
 
 
• A compound is a substance formed when two or more different elements chemically bond together.
 
• Compounds have properties different from the individual elements that make them up.
 
• Water (H₂O) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) are common examples of compounds.

questions.question: The Sir Creek dispute is a long-standing border dispute between India and which neighbouring country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sir Creek dispute is a territorial dispute between India and Pakistan, involving a marshy area in the Rann of Kutch region.
 
• Sir Creek is a 96-km strip of water disputed between India and Pakistan in the Arabian Sea.
 
• The dispute has its origins in the interpretation of the maritime boundary line between Sindh (Pakistan) and Gujarat (India) as per the 1914 agreement between the then government of Sindh and Rao Maharaj of Kutch.
 
• The Sir Creek issue has implications for the maritime boundaries and exclusive economic zones of both countries, affecting rights over fishing and potential undersea oil and gas reserves.
 
• Despite several rounds of talks, the dispute remains unresolved, with both nations holding differing interpretations of the boundary demarcation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)**

 
 
• An EEZ is a sea zone prescribed by the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) over which a state has special rights regarding the exploration and use of marine resources.
 
• It extends up to 200 nautical miles from the coast of the state in question.
 
• The Sir Creek dispute impacts the determination of the EEZ boundaries for India and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **UNCLOS**
 
 
• The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) is an international agreement that establishes a legal framework for all marine and maritime activities.
 
• It was signed in 1982 and came into force in 1994.
 
• Both India and Pakistan are signatories to UNCLOS, which influences their negotiations over the Sir Creek dispute.
 
 
 
• **Rann of Kutch**
 
 
• The Rann of Kutch is a large area of salt marshes located in the Thar Desert in the Kutch District of Gujarat, India, and the Sindh province of Pakistan.
 
• It is renowned for its unique geography and is one of the largest salt deserts in the world.
 
• The area is subject to seasonal flooding from the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• **Indus Waters Treaty**
 
 
• The Indus Waters Treaty is a water-distribution treaty between India and Pakistan, brokered by the World Bank and signed in 1960.
 
• It outlines the allocation of water resources from the Indus River and its tributaries.
 
• While not directly related to the Sir Creek dispute, it is another significant water-related agreement between the two countries.

questions.question: The main thinking part of the brain that receives sensory impulses from various receptors is the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fore-brain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The fore-brain is the largest and most complex part of the brain, responsible for various higher-order functions.
 
• It includes structures such as the cerebrum, thalamus, and hypothalamus.
 
• The cerebrum, a major part of the fore-brain, is involved in sensory perception, voluntary motor actions, and cognitive functions.
 
• The thalamus acts as a relay station, transmitting sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex.
 
• The hypothalamus controls autonomic functions and links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b9b3ceb4ec2845223ade9281a6837d6e3bcc038d4a7206f9ad2c6fbd095607a.png]

• **Mid-brain:**

 
 
• The mid-brain, or mesencephalon, is located between the fore-brain and hind-brain.
 
• It plays a crucial role in motor movement, particularly movements of the eye, and in auditory and visual processing.
 
• Structures within the mid-brain include the tectum and tegmentum.
 
 
 
• **Spinal Cord:**
 
 
• The spinal cord is part of the central nervous system that runs down the vertebral column.
 
• It transmits nerve signals between the brain and the rest of the body.
 
• It also coordinates reflexes and contains neural circuits that can independently control numerous basic reflexes and functions.
 
 
 
• **Hind-brain:**
 
 
• The hind-brain consists of structures such as the cerebellum, pons, and medulla oblongata.
 
• It is responsible for coordinating movement and balance, and controlling vital functions such as breathing and heart rate.
 
• The cerebellum is particularly important for motor control and coordination.

questions.question: A bought an item for ₹384 and sold it for ₹480. B bought another item for ₹1,254 and sold it for ₹1,672. What is the ratio of the gain percentage of A to the gain percentage of B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Gain % of **A** = (480 − 384) ÷ 384 × 100 = 96 ÷ 384 × 100 = 25%.

Gain % of **B** = (1672 − 1254) ÷ 1254 × 100 = 418 ÷ 1254 × 100 = 33.33% or (100/3)%.

**Ratio** = 25 ÷ (100/3) = 25 × 3 ÷ 100 = 75 ÷ 100 = 3/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CPA = ₹384, SPA = ₹480 | CPB = ₹1,254, SPB = ₹1,672.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/85e1f847aac0d5ca6019fa91bd480cc6c17deabafff0d6536433ef2abf3f9e1e.png] 

⇒ **Gain for A** = 480 − 384 = 96.

⇒ **Gain % of A (GA)** = (96 ÷ 384) × 100 = 25%.

⇒ **Gain for B** = 1672 − 1254 = 418.

⇒ **Gain % of B (GB)** = (418 ÷ 1254) × 100 = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = 100/3%.

⇒ **Ratio (GA : GB)** = 25 : (100/3) = 75 : 100 = 3 : 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/4.**

questions.question: Which of the following reactions is NOT an example of oxidation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Oxidation refers to the process where a substance loses electrons and increases its oxidation state.
 
• The reaction 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl2 involves the decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine gas.
 
• In this reaction, silver (Ag) is reduced (gains electrons), not oxidized.
 
• Chlorine (Cl2 ) is formed by the oxidation of chloride ions (Cl-), but silver itself does not undergo oxidation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation**

 
 
• It involves the loss of electrons from a substance, increasing in oxidation state.
 
• Common examples include the reaction of metals with oxygen to form oxides.
 
 
 
• **Reduction**
 
 
• Reduction is the gain of electrons by a substance, leading to a decrease in oxidation state.
 
• It often occurs alongside oxidation in redox (reduction-oxidation) reactions.
 
 
 
• **Redox Reactions**
 
 
• Redox reactions involve both reduction and oxidation processes occurring simultaneously.
 
• These reactions are fundamental to various biological and industrial processes.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Oxidation**
 
 
• Combustion of fuels: C + O2 → CO2
 
• Rusting of iron: 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3.

questions.question: Who was the first to use a glass prism to obtain a spectrum of sunlight?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Isaac Newton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Isaac Newton** was the first scientist to use a glass prism to obtain a spectrum of sunlight in the year **1666**.
 
• He conducted his experiments in his home in Woolsthorpe, England, during the **Great Plague**.
 
• Newton discovered that white light is composed of a spectrum of colors, which can be separated using a prism.
 
• His work laid the foundation for the study of optics and the understanding of the nature of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prism**

 
 
• A prism is a transparent optical element with flat, polished surfaces that refract light.
 
• Prisms can be used to break light up into its constituent spectral colors (the colors of the rainbow).
 
 
 
• **Optics**
 
 
• Optics is the branch of physics that studies the behavior and properties of light.
 
• It includes the study of reflection, refraction, dispersion, and diffraction of light.
 
 
 
• **Spectrum**
 
 
• A spectrum refers to the range of different colors produced when light is dispersed by a prism.
 
• The visible spectrum includes all the colors that can be seen by the human eye, ranging from red to violet.
 
 
 
• **Great Plague**
 
 
• The Great Plague (1665-1666) was the last major epidemic of the bubonic plague to occur in England.
 
• During this period, many universities closed, and Isaac Newton returned to his home in Woolsthorpe, where he conducted his groundbreaking experiments.

questions.question: Consider a situation where a person is sitting in a car and is driving at a constant velocity in a straight line. If the car turns sharply to the left, the person will be pushed in which of the following directions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a car makes a sharp turn, the passengers inside experience a force due to inertia.
 
• This force is a result of the body's tendency to maintain its state of motion, as per Newton's First Law of Motion.
 
• If the car turns left, inertia causes the person to be pushed towards the right.
 
• This perceived force pushing the person to the right is often referred to as a "centrifugal force" in a non-inertial reference frame.
 
• The actual cause is the car moving left while the person's body tends to continue in a straight line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion (Law of Inertia)**

 
 
• States that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• This law explains why passengers move in the opposite direction of the turn.
 
 
 
• **Centrifugal Force**
 
 
• It is a perceived force that acts outward on a body moving around a center, arising from the body's inertia.
 
• It is not a real force but rather a result of the inertia of the body in a rotating reference frame.
 
 
 
• **Inertial Reference Frame**
 
 
• A frame of reference in which Newton's laws of motion hold true.
 
• In such frames, objects not acted upon by forces move in straight lines at constant speeds.
 
 
 
• **Non-Inertial Reference Frame**
 
 
• A frame of reference that is accelerating or rotating.
 
• In these frames, fictitious forces, such as centrifugal force, are introduced to explain motion.

questions.question: Which of the following will be the average velocity of the particle with initial velocity u and final velocity v in the given time interval?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(u+v)/2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Average velocity is defined as the total displacement divided by the total time taken.
 
• For a particle with constant acceleration, the average velocity over a time interval can be calculated using the initial and final velocities.
 
• The formula for average velocity (v_avg) in this context is given by: v_avg = (u + v) / 2.
 
• Here, 'u' represents the initial velocity and 'v' represents the final velocity of the particle.
 
• This formula is derived from the kinematic equations of motion in classical mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Velocity:** It is a vector quantity that refers to the rate at which an object changes its position. It has both magnitude and direction.
 
• **Displacement:** This is a vector quantity that refers to the overall change in position of an object. It is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of the object.
 
• **Acceleration:** It is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time. It can be positive (speeding up) or negative (slowing down).
 
• **Kinematic Equations:** These are equations that describe the motion of objects under the influence of constant acceleration. They are used to calculate displacement, velocity, and time.
 
• **Uniform Motion:** This refers to motion at a constant speed in a straight line. For such motion, the average velocity is simply the constant velocity.

questions.question: Two pipes A and B together can fill a cistern in 4 hours. Had they been opened separately, then B would have taken 6 hours more than A to fill the cistern. How much time will be taken by A to fill the cistern separately?

Combined time = (A × B) ÷ (A + B)

Combined time = (6 × 12) ÷ (6 + 12) = 72 ÷ 18 = 4 hr.

Since this matches the given data, the choice is correct.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hr.**

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 1000 litres in 5 hours and 6 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 1800 litres?

questions.question: In a circuit, a 10 volt battery and three resistors R1 = 2Ω, R2 = 3Ω, and R3 = 6Ω are connected in parallel to each other. Which of the following is the correct value of effective resistance Rₑ and current I flowing through the circuit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Re = 1Ω, I = 10 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The given circuit consists of a 10V battery and three resistors (R1 = 2Ω, R2 = 3Ω, R3 = 6Ω) connected in parallel.
 
• In a parallel circuit, the effective resistance (Re) can be calculated using the formula: 1/Re = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3.
 
• Using the given values: 1/Re = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1Ω.
 
• The total current (I) in the circuit can be calculated using Ohm's law: I = V/Re.
 
• With V = 10V and Re = 1Ω, the total current I = 10V / 1Ω = 10A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law**

 
 
• States that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is given by: V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
 
 
• **Series vs. Parallel Circuits**
 
 
• In series circuits, resistors are connected end-to-end, so the current is the same through each resistor.
 
• In parallel circuits, resistors are connected across the same two points, so the voltage is the same across each resistor.
 
 
 
• **Effective Resistance in Parallel**
 
 
• The effective resistance of resistors in parallel is always less than the smallest individual resistor in the network.
 
• This is because the total current through the circuit is the sum of the currents through each resistor.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Parallel Circuits**
 
 
• Used in household electrical wiring to ensure that appliances operate independently.
 
• Commonly found in the automotive industry for connecting various electrical components like lights and sensors.

questions.question: In which of the following organisms is fragmentation common?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only a few multicellular organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fragmentation is a type of asexual reproduction common in certain multicellular organisms.
 
• It is especially prevalent among organisms such as sponges, some annelid worms, and sea stars.
 
• During fragmentation, an organism breaks into fragments, each capable of growing independently into a new organism.
 
• This method allows rapid population expansion in favorable conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction**

 
 
• It is a mode of reproduction where offspring arise from a single organism.
 
• It does not involve the fusion of gametes, and the offspring are genetically identical to the parent.
 
• Common methods include binary fission, budding, fragmentation, and spore formation.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission**
 
 
• A form of asexual reproduction most commonly observed in prokaryotic organisms like bacteria.
 
• The parent organism divides into two equal-sized daughter cells.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• Another form of asexual reproduction where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• It is commonly seen in yeast and some invertebrates like hydra.
 
 
 
• **Spore Formation**
 
 
• Involves the formation of spores that can develop into new individuals.
 
• Commonly observed in fungi, algae, and some plants.

questions.question: The average of eight numbers is 14. The average of six of these numbers is 16. The average of the remaining two numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Net deviation** must be zero.

Average of 8 numbers = 14. **Deviation** for 6 numbers = 6 × (16 − 14) = +12.

To balance, deviation for remaining 2 numbers = −12.

Average of remaining 2 numbers = 14 + (−12 ÷ 2) = 14 − 6 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59c1453f4bf3e4e00f1a20ba05ccb3687ae44721864658423ffa2c9abb619dfd.png] 

**Given:** Average of **8 numbers** = 14, Average of **6 numbers** = 16.

**Formula Used:** Sum = Average × Number of terms

⇒ Total sum of 8 numbers = 8 × 14 = 112

⇒ Sum of 6 numbers = 6 × 16 = 96

⇒ Sum of remaining 2 numbers = 112 − 96 = 16

⇒ Average of remaining 2 numbers = 16 ÷ 2 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, the total average A = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and a is the average.

Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This is useful for finding missing values in a data set.</p

questions.question: Which of the following contracts and relaxes to cause movement and contains special proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muscles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Muscles** are tissues that contract and relax to cause movement in the body.
 
• They contain special proteins called **actin and myosin** that facilitate contraction and relaxation.
 
• There are three types of muscles in the human body: **skeletal, smooth, and cardiac** muscles.
 
• Skeletal muscles are primarily responsible for **voluntary movements** such as walking, running, and lifting.
 
• Muscles work in pairs; while one muscle contracts, the other relaxes, enabling smooth and controlled movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Actin and Myosin**

 
 
• These are the primary proteins involved in muscle contraction.
 
• Actin forms thin filaments, while myosin forms thick filaments within muscle fibers.
 
• The interaction between actin and myosin filaments is crucial for muscle contraction.
 
• This interaction is powered by ATP (adenosine triphosphate), the energy currency of cells.
 
 
 
• **Skeletal Muscles**
 
 
• They are attached to bones by tendons and are under voluntary control.
 
• Skeletal muscles are striated, meaning they have a banded appearance.
 
• They are responsible for locomotion and other body movements.
 
 
 
• **Smooth Muscles**
 
 
• These muscles are found in the walls of internal organs such as the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels.
 
• Smooth muscles are not under voluntary control and are responsible for involuntary movements.
 
• They are non-striated and have a smooth appearance.
 
 
 
• **Cardiac Muscles**
 
 
• Cardiac muscles are found exclusively in the heart.
 
• They are responsible for pumping blood throughout the body.
 
• Cardiac muscles are striated like skeletal muscles but are involuntary like smooth muscles.

questions.question: According to the sign convention, the focal length of a convex lens is _______ and that of a concave lens is _____
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**positive; negative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the sign convention used in optics, the focal length of a convex lens is considered **positive**.
 
• Conversely, the focal length of a concave lens is considered **negative**.
 
• This sign convention is based on the Cartesian coordinate system, where distances measured in the direction of the incident light (rightward) are positive, and those measured against it (leftward) are negative.
 
• The convex lens, being converging, focuses parallel rays of light to a point on the positive side of the lens, hence the positive focal length.
 
• The concave lens, being diverging, makes parallel rays of light appear to diverge from a point on the negative side of the lens, hence the negative focal length.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Lens**

 
 
• A convex lens is thicker at the center than at the edges.
 
• It converges light rays that are initially parallel, bringing them to a focus.
 
• Commonly used in magnifying glasses, cameras, and corrective lenses for hyperopia (farsightedness).
 
 
 
• **Concave Lens**
 
 
• A concave lens is thinner at the center than at the edges.
 
• It diverges light rays that are initially parallel, making them spread out.
 
• Commonly used in corrective lenses for myopia (nearsightedness).
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention in Optics**
 
 
• Distances measured in the direction of the incident light are taken as positive.
 
• Distances measured against the direction of the incident light are taken as negative.
 
• This convention helps in the systematic analysis of image formation by lenses and mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length**
 
 
• The focal length of a lens is the distance between the center of the lens and its focal point.
 
• It is a critical parameter in determining the imaging properties of the lens.
 
• In convex lenses, the focal length is positive, and in concave lenses, it is negative as per the sign convention.

questions.question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a train is 45 km/h and including stoppages, it is 36 km/h. How many minutes does the train stop per hour?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Stoppage time per hour = (Difference in speeds ÷ Speed excluding stoppages) × 60 minutes

Difference in speeds = 45 − 36 = 9 km/h

Stoppage time = (9 ÷ 45) × 60 = (1/5) × 60 = 12 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/580fc193a02c124eebff576c97dc1d2d455084b8318fcdb158742c6c946b11a7.png] 

**Given:**

Speed excluding stoppages = 45 km/h

Speed including stoppages = 36 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ In 1 hour, the train covers 36 km when including stoppages.

⇒ Without stoppages, the train would cover 45 km in 60 minutes.

⇒ To cover 36 km without stoppages, time taken = (36 ÷ 45) × 60 minutes

⇒ Time taken = (4/5) × 60 = 48 minutes

⇒ Stoppage time = 60 minutes − 48 minutes

⇒ Stoppage time = 12 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. When including stoppages, the total time increases, thereby reducing the average speed.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. For opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: How many isotopes of hydrogen element exist in nature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hydrogen has three naturally occurring isotopes: protium (¹H), deuterium (²H), and tritium (³H).
 
• Protium is the most abundant isotope, comprising about 99.98% of hydrogen found in nature.
 
• Deuterium, also known as heavy hydrogen, accounts for about 0.02% of natural hydrogen and is used in heavy water reactors.
 
• Tritium is radioactive and is found in trace amounts in nature, primarily produced by the interaction of cosmic rays with the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes**

 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a particular chemical element that differ in neutron number, and consequently in nucleon number.
 
• All isotopes of an element have the same number of protons in each atom.
 
 
 
• **Protium (¹H)**
 
 
• Protium has one proton and no neutrons in its nucleus.
 
• It is the most common isotope of hydrogen.
 
 
 
• **Deuterium (²H)**
 
 
• Deuterium has one proton and one neutron in its nucleus.
 
• It is used in nuclear reactors and scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Tritium (³H)**
 
 
• Tritium has one proton and two neutrons in its nucleus.
 
• It is radioactive and has a half-life of about 12.3 years.
 
• Used in thermonuclear weapons and as a tracer in biochemical research.

questions.question: In ΔABC if ∠A = 50° and ∠B = 70°, find the measure of exterior angle A.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Exterior angle at any vertex of a triangle is the **sum of the two opposite interior angles**.

Exterior ∠A = ∠B + ∠C

First find ∠C = 180° − (50° + 70°) = 60°.

Exterior ∠A = 70° + 60° = 130°.

**∴ The correct answer is 130°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠A = 50°, ∠B = 70°

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles on a straight line is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e07a3d7b61f1ad6d57b0a6da5545b5531c6c40242792a8f6692a4e40d6bae97f.png] 

In ΔABC, interior **∠A = 50°**.

The interior angle and the exterior angle at the same vertex form a **linear pair**.

⇒ Interior ∠A + Exterior ∠A = 180°

⇒ 50° + Exterior ∠A = 180°

⇒ Exterior ∠A = 180° − 50°

⇒ Exterior ∠A = 130°

**∴ The correct answer is 130°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Linear Pair Postulate

If two angles form a linear pair, then they are supplementary, meaning their sum is exactly 180°.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is always 180° (∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°).</p

questions.question: With an initial velocity of 10 m/s, an object is thrown vertically upwards. The maximum height attained by the object is (Assume g = 10m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is thrown vertically upwards, it decelerates under the influence of gravity (g = 10 m/s²).
 
• The initial velocity (u) of the object is given as 10 m/s.
 
• At the maximum height, the final velocity (v) is 0 m/s.
 
• Using the equation of motion: v²=u²-2gh, we can calculate the maximum height (h).
 
• Substituting the values, 0=10²-2times 10times h, solving this gives h=5m meters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equations of Motion**

 
 
• These are used to describe the relationship between the velocity, acceleration, and displacement of an object.
 
• The three primary equations of motion are: v=u+at, s=ut+(1)/(2)at², and v²=u²+2as.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Acceleration (g)**
 
 
• It is the acceleration due to gravity, typically taken as 9.8 m/s² or approximated to 10 m/s² for simplicity in calculations.
 
• This value indicates how fast an object accelerates when falling freely under the influence of gravity.
 
 
 
• **Maximum Height of a Projectile**
 
 
• The maximum height is the highest point reached by an object projected upwards.
 
• At this point, the vertical component of the object's velocity is zero.
 
 
 
• **Vertical Projectile Motion**
 
 
• When an object is projected vertically upwards, it moves against the gravity until it reaches a point where the velocity becomes zero.
 
• It then starts descending under the influence of gravity, retracing its path.

questions.question: According to the reactivity series of metals, which metal pair is found in native state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold and platinum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gold and platinum are found in their native state due to their low reactivity.
 
• They are part of the noble metals group, which resist oxidation and corrosion.
 
• Gold and platinum are often found in their elemental form in nature, not combined with other elements.
 
• These metals are less likely to form compounds with other elements, which is why they are found in pure form.
 
• Both metals have been used historically in coinage, jewelry, and industrial applications due to their stability and rarity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series of Metals**

 
 
• The reactivity series arranges metals in order of their reactivity from highest to lowest.
 
• Metals higher in the series, like potassium and sodium, are more reactive and readily form compounds.
 
• Metals lower in the series, like gold and platinum, are less reactive and often found in their native state.
 
• The reactivity series helps predict how metals will react with acids, water, and other substances.
 
 
 
• **Native State**
 
 
• A native state refers to metals found in nature in their pure, elemental form.
 
• Metals like gold, silver, and platinum are typically found in their native state due to their resistance to corrosion and oxidation.
 
• Finding metals in their native state was historically significant for early human societies, leading to the development of metallurgy.
 
 
 
• **Noble Metals**
 
 
• Noble metals include gold, platinum, and other metals resistant to corrosion and oxidation.
 
• They are called "noble" due to their stability and rarity.
 
• Noble metals are used in various high-value applications, including electronics, jewelry, and catalytic converters.
 
 
 
• **Industrial and Historical Significance**
 
 
• Gold and platinum have been valued throughout history for their beauty and rarity.
 
• Both metals have significant industrial applications due to their conductive and catalytic properties.
 
• Gold is widely used in electronics for its excellent conductivity and resistance to tarnish.
 
• Platinum is crucial in the automotive industry for catalytic converters, reducing harmful emissions.

questions.question: Express 0.overline{512} in the form (p)/(q), where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To convert a **pure recurring decimal** to a fraction, write the **repeating digits** as the numerator.

For the denominator, write the digit **9** as many times as there are **repeating digits** in the decimal part.

Here, the repeating part is **512**, which has **three digits**.

∴ The fraction is 512 ÷ 999.

questions.question: The ratio between the radius of the base and the height of a cylinder is 3: 4. If its volume is 38808 cm³ then, using π = (22)/(7) find the diameter of the cylinder.

Ratio of **radius (r)** to **height (h)** = 3 : 4 ⇒ Let r = 3x and h = 4x.

Volume = πr²h = (22/7) × (3x)² × 4x = 38808.

⇒ (22/7) × 9x² × 4x = 38808 ⇒ x³ = (38808 × 7) ÷ (22 × 36) = 343.

⇒ x = √³(343) = 7.

**Diameter** = 2r = 2 × 3x = 6 × 7 = 42 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 cm.**

⇒ Let r = 3x and h = 4x.

⇒ 38808 = (22/7) × (3x)² × 4x

⇒ 38808 = (22/7) × 9x² × 4x

⇒ 38808 = (22 × 36 × x³) / 7

⇒ x³ = (38808 × 7) / 792

⇒ x³ = 49 × 7 = 343

⇒ x = 7

⇒ Radius (r) = 3 × 7 = 21 cm

Volume Ratios

questions.question: If the position of an object is in between the principal focus and pole of a concave mirror, then the image formed will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**virtual, erect and enlarged**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed between the principal focus (F) and the pole (P) of a concave mirror, the image formed is virtual.
 
• The image is erect, meaning it is upright relative to the object.
 
• The image is also enlarged, making it appear bigger than the actual object.
 
• This phenomenon occurs because the light rays diverge after reflection and appear to come from a point behind the mirror.
 
• This property is utilized in applications like shaving mirrors and makeup mirrors where a magnified upright image is desired.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror that curves inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• It converges light rays that are incident parallel to its principal axis after reflecting them.
 
• It has applications in devices such as telescopes, head mirrors in medical examinations, and in vehicle headlights to focus light.
 
 
 
• **Principal Focus:**
 
 
• The principal focus of a concave mirror is the point where light rays parallel to the principal axis converge after reflection.
 
• It is located on the principal axis, midway between the mirror's surface and the center of curvature.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation by Mirrors:**
 
 
• The nature of the image (real or virtual, erect or inverted, magnified or diminished) depends on the position of the object relative to the mirror.
 
• Concave mirrors can form real and inverted images or virtual and erect images based on the object's placement.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Equation:**
 
 
• The relationship between the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) of a spherical mirror is given by the mirror equation: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v.
 
• This equation helps in determining the position and nature of the image formed by the mirror.

questions.question: Who among the following discovered the nucleus of an atom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**E Rutherford**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ernest Rutherford** discovered the nucleus of an atom in 1911 through his famous **gold foil experiment**.
 
• Rutherford's experiment showed that **most of the atom is empty space** with a small, dense, positively charged nucleus at its center.
 
• He proposed the **Rutherford model of the atom**, which described the atom as having a central nucleus surrounded by electrons.
 
• Rutherford's discovery laid the foundation for the modern understanding of atomic structure and helped in the development of the Bohr model of the atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gold Foil Experiment:**

 
 
• Conducted by Rutherford in 1909 with the help of his students Geiger and Marsden.
 
• Involved bombarding a thin gold foil with alpha particles.
 
• Showed that most alpha particles passed through the foil, but some were deflected at large angles, indicating a dense central nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Rutherford Model of the Atom:**
 
 
• Proposed in 1911 following the gold foil experiment.
 
• Described the atom as a small, dense nucleus surrounded by orbiting electrons.
 
• Challenged the previous plum pudding model proposed by J.J. Thomson.
 
 
 
• **Subatomic Particles:**
 
 
• Protons: Positively charged particles found in the nucleus.
 
• Neutrons: Neutral particles found in the nucleus, discovered by James Chadwick in 1932.
 
• Electrons: Negatively charged particles orbiting the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Rutherford's Contributions:**
 
 
• Considered the father of nuclear physics.
 
• Won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1908 for his work on the disintegration of elements and the chemistry of radioactive substances.
 
• Discovered the concept of radioactive half-life.

questions.question:
Which of the following substances is in solid form in the given reaction?

Sodium sulphate + barium chloride → sodium chloride + barium sulphate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barium sulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Barium sulphate is the product that forms as a precipitate in the reaction between sodium sulphate and barium chloride.
 
• It is an insoluble compound in water, leading to its solid formation in the reaction mixture.
 
• The chemical equation for the reaction is: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → 2 NaCl + BaSO₄.
 
• In this reaction, barium sulphate (BaSO₄) is the only substance that precipitates out, i.e., forms a solid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precipitation Reaction**

 
 
• A precipitation reaction occurs when two soluble salts react in aqueous solution to form one or more insoluble products (precipitates).
 
• Barium sulphate is a common precipitate used in laboratory experiments to demonstrate precipitation reactions.
 
 
 
• **Solubility Rules**
 
 
• Solubility rules help predict whether a substance will dissolve or form a precipitate in water.
 
• Sulphates are generally soluble, except for those of barium, lead, and calcium.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Barium Sulphate**
 
 
• It is used as a radiopaque agent in medical imaging of the digestive system.
 
• It is also used in the manufacturing of paints, coatings, and plastics as a white pigment and filler.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Equation Balancing**
 
 
• Balancing chemical equations ensures the conservation of mass where the number of atoms for each element is the same on both sides of the equation.
 
• This reaction is balanced with the formula: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → 2 NaCl + BaSO₄.

questions.question: The fourth proportional to 15, 10 and 12 is:
questions.solution:

**Given:** Three numbers are **15, 10, and 12**.

**Formula Used:** If **a, b, c, and x** are in **proportion**, then **a : b :: c : x**, which means **a/b = c/x**.

Let the **fourth proportional** be **x**.

⇒ 15 : 10 = 12 : x

⇒ 15 ÷ 10 = 12 ÷ x

⇒ 15x = 120

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is given by the formula **√(a × b)**.

Third Proportional

The third proportional to two numbers **a** and **b** is defined as the value **c** such that **a : b = b : c**, calculated as **c = b² ÷ a**.

Direct Proportion

Two quantities are in direct proportion if an increase in one leads to a proportional increase in the other, expressed as **x/y = k**.</p

questions.question: The reproductive parts of angiosperms are located in the flower, where the female reproductive part is made of three parts, stigma, style and ovary and is known as:

• The stigma is the sticky top part that **collects pollen grains**.
 
• The style is a tube-like structure that **supports the stigma** and connects it to the ovary.

• **Sepal**

• They are usually green and **protect the flower bud** before it opens.
 
 
 
• **Petal**

questions.question: The atomic mass of an element is usually expressed in which of the following units?

__
 
• Atomic mass units (amu) are the standard unit of mass that quantifies the mass of an atom or molecule.
 
• 1 amu is defined as one twelfth (1/12) of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
 
• The atomic mass unit allows chemists to compare the masses of different atoms on a scale that is easy to use and understand.
 
• The unit is widely used in chemistry and physics to express atomic and molecular weights.
 
• Atomic mass units are essential for understanding chemical reactions, molecular structures, and isotopic compositions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes:**

 
 
• Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons and thus different atomic masses.
 
• Examples include Carbon-12, Carbon-13, and Carbon-14.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass:**
 
 
• The mass of one mole of a substance (usually expressed in g/mol).
 
• It is numerically equal to the atomic or molecular mass in amu but expressed in grams.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Number:**
 
 
• The number of atoms, ions, or molecules in one mole of a substance, approximately 6.022 x 10²³.
 
• This constant is used to convert between atomic mass units and grams.
 
 
 
• **Relative Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• A weighted average of the atomic masses of an element's isotopes.
 
• It reflects the abundance of each isotope in nature.

questions.question: Which of the following in eukaryotes is separated from the cytoplasm by a double-layered membrane and it directs the life processes of the cell?

• The nucleus in eukaryotic cells is separated from the cytoplasm by a double-layered membrane called the nuclear envelope.
 
• The nucleus houses the cell's DNA and is the control center for the cell, directing all cellular activities including growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• The nuclear envelope contains nuclear pores that regulate the exchange of materials between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
 
• Inside the nucleus, the DNA is organized into structures called chromosomes, which contain the genetic instructions for the development and function of the organism.
 
• The nucleolus, a structure within the nucleus, is responsible for producing ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and assembling ribosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribosome:**

 
 
• Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for synthesizing proteins by translating messenger RNA (mRNA).
 
• They can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.
 
 
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):**
 
 
• The ER is a network of membranes involved in protein and lipid synthesis.
 
• It is classified into two types: rough ER (with ribosomes) and smooth ER (without ribosomes).
 
 
 
• **Plastids:**
 
 
• Plastids are organelles found in plant cells and algae.
 
• They are responsible for functions such as photosynthesis (chloroplasts), storage of products (amyloplasts), and synthesis of compounds (chromoplasts).
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Envelope:**
 
 
• The nuclear envelope is a double membrane that encloses the nucleus.
 
• It contains nuclear pores that control the movement of substances between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

questions.question: If the volume of a cuboid is 3x² - 27, then its possible dimensions are:

Factorize the **volume expression** directly to find the dimensions.

Volume = 3x² − 27

Take common factor 3: 3(x² − 9)

Apply identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b): 3(x − 3)(x + 3)

**∴ The correct answer is 3, x − 3, x + 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Volume = 3(x² − 9)

⇒ Volume = 3(x² − 3²)

⇒ Using identity **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)**

⇒ Volume = 3 × (x − 3) × (x + 3)

⇒ Possible dimensions are 3, (x − 3), and (x + 3).

Volume of Cuboid

The volume of a cuboid is the product of its three dimensions: length (l), breadth (b), and height (h). V = l × b × h.

Factorization Method

To find dimensions from a polynomial volume, factorize the polynomial into three linear or constant factors.</p

questions.question: In order to pass in an examination, a student is required to get 975 marks out of the maximum aggregate marks. Priya got 870 marks and was declared failed by 7%. What is the maximum aggregate marks that a student can get in the examination?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Passing Marks** required = 975

**Priya Marks** obtained = 870

**Deficit marks** = 975 − 870 = 105

Given 7% = 105 marks ⇒ 1% = 15 marks

**Maximum Marks** (100%) = 15 × 100 = 1500

**∴ The correct answer is 1500.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89e9466d136fb791d57aa123ad24746ede2a5dc9ea1298250285d8b25de53863.png] 

**Given:**

**Passing Marks** = 975

**Marks obtained by Priya** = 870

**Failure Margin (in %)** = 7%

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Difference in marks** = Passing Marks − Obtained Marks

⇒ Difference = 975 − 870 = 105

⇒ According to the question, this difference is 7% of the maximum marks.

⇒ 7% of **Maximum Marks (M)** = 105

⇒ (7 ÷ 100) × M = 105

⇒ M = (105 × 100) ÷ 7

⇒ M = 15 × 100

⇒ M = 1500

**∴ The correct answer is 1500.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Calculation

To find the whole value (100%) when a certain percentage (x%) is known as value V: Total = (V ÷ x) × 100.

Pass Percentage

Pass % = (Passing Marks ÷ Maximum Marks) × 100. In this case, (975 ÷ 1500) × 100 = 65%.

Score Gap Analysis

If a student fails by x marks and another passes by y marks over the passing limit, the gap between their scores is (x + y).</p

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 7: 5. If their positive difference is 360, then the greater number between them is:
questions.solution:

Ratio of numbers = 7 : 5

Difference in ratio units = 7 − 5 = 2 units

2 units → 360 ⇒ 1 unit = 180

Greater number (7 units) = 7 × 180 = 1260

**∴ The correct answer is 1260.**

**Given:**

Ratio of numbers = 7 : 5

⇒ Greater number = 7x = 7 × 180

⇒ Greater number = 1260

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

A ratio compares two quantities. If a : b = c : d, then product of extremes (a×d) equals product of means (b×c).

questions.question: Who developed the planetary model of the atom with electrons orbiting the nucleus in discrete energy levels?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Niels Bohr developed the planetary model of the atom in 1913.
 
• In Bohr's model, electrons orbit the nucleus in discrete energy levels without radiating energy.

• **Rutherford's Model:**
 
 
• Proposed by Ernest Rutherford in 1911, the model depicted the atom as having a small, dense nucleus positively charged with electrons orbiting around it.
 
• It could not explain the stability of electron orbits, as classical physics predicted that electrons would spiral into the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Energy Levels:**
 
 
• In Bohr's model, electrons occupy fixed energy levels or shells around the nucleus.

• **Electron Configuration:**
 
 
• The arrangement of electrons in an atom's energy levels is known as electron configuration.
 
• Electron configuration determines the chemical properties of an element.
 
• Bohr's model provided a simple way to understand how electrons are distributed in atoms.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an object moving in uniform circular motion?

options.text: A bird flying in the sky

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A satellite in a circular orbit around the earth.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A satellite in a circular orbit around the earth is an example of uniform circular motion because it moves at a constant speed along a circular path.
 
• The centripetal force required to maintain the satellite's circular motion is provided by the gravitational pull of the Earth.
 
• The satellite's velocity remains constant in magnitude but its direction continuously changes, resulting in a circular trajectory.
 
• This type of motion is characterized by a constant angular velocity and a constant distance from the center of the Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centripetal Force:**

 
 
• It is the force that acts on a body moving in a circular path, directed towards the center around which the body is moving.
 
• In the case of a satellite, this force is provided by the gravitational attraction of the Earth.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Force:**
 
 
• It is the attractive force that exists between any two masses.
 
• For satellites orbiting the Earth, this force ensures they stay in orbit.
 
 
 
• **Angular Velocity:**
 
 
• It is the rate of change of the angle through which the body moves on a circular path.
 
• In uniform circular motion, the angular velocity remains constant.
 
 
 
• **Orbital Speed:**
 
 
• It is the constant speed at which a satellite must travel to stay in a stable orbit around a planet.
 
• The orbital speed depends on the mass of the planet and the distance of the satellite from the planet's center.

questions.question: If the radius of sphere is decreased by 10 percent, then the volume of sphere will be decreased by what percentage?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Radius** decrease = 10% → **Fractional value** = 1/10.

**Initial Radius** : **Final Radius** = 10 : 9.

**Volume** ∝ **Radius³** ⇒ Ratio of Volume = (10)³ : (9)³ = 1000 : 729.

**Decrease in Volume** = ((1000 − 729) ÷ 1000) × 100 = 271 ÷ 10 = 27.1%.

**∴ The correct answer is 27.1%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13050cea4421626493cc4bd7ede708dfc87c530c0459189d2926e878af557efd.png] 

**Given:** Percentage decrease in **Radius** (r) = 10%.

**Formula Used:** Volume of Sphere = (4/3) × π × r³.

**Net Percentage Change** for three successive changes of x%, y%, and z%:

⇒ First two changes: a = x + y + (x × y)/100

⇒ Final change: Net = a + z + (a × z)/100

⇒ Here, x = y = z = −10 (negative sign denotes decrease).

⇒ First two: (−10) + (−10) + (−10 × −10)/100 = −20 + 1 = −19%.

⇒ Final: (−19) + (−10) + (−19 × −10)/100 = −29 + 1.9 = −27.1%.

**∴ The correct answer is 27.1%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Surface Area Change

The **Surface Area** of a sphere is proportional to r². If radius decreases by 10%, area decreases by 10 + 10 − (10 × 10)/100 = 19%.

Successive Percentage Rule

For a 3D figure, the volume change depends on three dimensions. For a sphere, all three dimensions are the same radius (r × r × r).

Volume of Hemisphere

The percentage change in volume remains the same for a **Hemisphere** (2/3 π r³) as it also depends on r³.</p

questions.question: If 75% of x is 15 less than 15% of 1500, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**15% of 1500** = 15 × 15 = 225.

Subtract 15: 225 − 15 = 210.

Given **75% of x** (which is 3/4 of x) = 210.

x = 210 × (4/3) = 70 × 4 = 280.

**∴ The correct answer is 280.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4332ffc423918e391a3923bc265f95786c9d74071c7c388ffb8a6a1d33c63fc.png] 

**Given:**

**Value 1** = 15% of 1500

**Value 2** = 75% of x

**Condition:** 75% of x = (15% of 1500) − 15

**Calculations:**

⇒ 15% of 1500 = (15/100) × 1500 = 15 × 15 = 225

⇒ 75% of x = 225 − 15

⇒ 0.75 × x = 210

⇒ x = 210 ÷ 0.75

⇒ x = 210 ÷ (3/4) = (210 × 4) ÷ 3

⇒ x = 70 × 4 = 280

**∴ The correct answer is 280.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting percentages to simple fractions like 75% = 3/4 or 25% = 1/4 speeds up calculation significantly.

Percentage Change Base

x% of y is always equal to y% of x. For example, 15% of 1500 is the same as 1500% of 15.

Linear Equation Formulation

Always translate verbal phrases like 'less than' or 'more than' into direct subtraction or addition from the base value.</p

questions.question: If blood :: connective tissue, then bones :: ________.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Both blood and bones are categorized under **connective tissues** in the human body.
 
• Connective tissue primarily serves to **support and bind other tissues** in the body.
 
• Blood, as a connective tissue, plays a vital role in **transporting oxygen, nutrients, and waste products** throughout the body.
 
• Bones, another type of connective tissue, provide **structural support, protection of organs, and facilitation of movement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Connective Tissue**

 
 
• Connective tissue is one of the four basic types of animal tissues, along with epithelial, muscular, and nervous tissues.
 
• It develops from the mesoderm, one of the three primary germ layers in the very early embryo.
 
• It is characterized by an extracellular matrix that separates the cells of the tissue.
 
• Types of connective tissue include loose connective tissue, dense connective tissue, cartilage, bone, and blood.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Connective Tissue**
 
 
• Provides structural support to other tissues and organs.
 
• Protects and insulates internal organs.
 
• Stores energy reserves in the form of fat.
 
• Transports substances throughout the body via blood.
 
• Defends the body against pathogens through the immune response.
 
 
 
• **Bone Tissue**
 
 
• Bone tissue, or osseous tissue, is a hard, dense connective tissue that forms the structural elements of the skeleton.
 
• It is composed of cells called osteocytes and a mineralized matrix that includes calcium phosphate.
 
• Bones support and protect various organs of the body, produce red and white blood cells, and store minerals.
 
• Bone remodeling is a continuous process where mature bone tissue is removed and new bone tissue is formed.
 
 
 
• **Blood as a Connective Tissue**
 
 
• Blood is considered a connective tissue because it has a matrix (plasma) and originates from the mesoderm layer of the embryo.
 
• It consists of red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma.
 
• Blood has several functions including transportation of gases, nutrients, and waste products, regulation of body temperature, and protection against diseases.

questions.question: The total amount of electric charge that flows through a circuit is 1200 C in 2 min. Then the amount of electric current that is drawn by the same electric circuit is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The total electric charge (Q) that flows through the circuit is given as 1200 Coulombs (C).
 
• The time (t) taken for this charge to flow is 2 minutes, which is equivalent to 120 seconds (2 min x 60 sec/min).
 
• Electric current (I) is calculated using the formula I = Q / t.
 
• Substituting the given values, I = 1200 C / 120 s = 10 A.
 
• Thus, the electric current drawn by the circuit is 10 Amperes (A).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Current:**

 
 
• Electric current is the flow of electric charge in a circuit.
 
• It is measured in Amperes (A), where 1 Ampere is equal to 1 Coulomb of charge passing through a point in 1 second.
 
 
 
• **Coulomb (C):**
 
 
• A Coulomb is the unit of electric charge in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• It is defined as the amount of charge transported by a constant current of one Ampere in one second.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Electric Current:**
 
 
• The formula to calculate electric current is I = Q / t, where I is the current, Q is the charge, and t is the time.
 
• This relationship helps in determining the current when the charge and time are known.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT true about the principal focus of a spherical mirror?

i) It always lies on the principal axis.

ii) An incident ray passing through the focus after reflection becomes parallel to the principal axis.

iii) Principal focus is a point where all the incident rays after reflection from the mirror meet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The principal focus of a spherical mirror always lies on the principal axis.
 
• An incident ray passing through the focus, after reflection, becomes parallel to the principal axis.
 
• Principal focus is defined as the point where rays parallel to the principal axis, after reflection, either converge (concave mirror) or appear to diverge from (convex mirror).
 
• Statement (iii) is incorrect because not all incident rays, after reflection, meet at the principal focus. Only rays parallel to the principal axis do.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror that curves inward like a spoon.
 
• It converges light rays to a point and is used in applications like telescopes, flashlights, and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror:**
 
 
• A convex mirror is a spherical mirror that curves outward.
 
• It diverges light rays and is commonly used for rearview mirrors in vehicles and security purposes.
 
 
 
• **Principal Axis:**
 
 
• The principal axis is the straight line passing through the center of curvature and the pole of the mirror.
 
• It is the reference line for defining the position of the principal focus and other points related to mirror reflection.
 
 
 
• **Center of Curvature:**
 
 
• The center of curvature is the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part.
 
• It lies on the principal axis and is denoted by the letter 'C'.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length:**
 
 
• Focal length is the distance between the pole and the principal focus of the mirror.
 
• It is half of the radius of curvature for a spherical mirror.

questions.question: What is the power of this combination of lens placed together when the power of the converging lens is 4.50 D and diverging lens is 3.00 D?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The power of a combination of lenses is the algebraic sum of the powers of individual lenses.
 
• The power of a converging lens (convex lens) is given as +4.50 D.
 
• The power of a diverging lens (concave lens) is given as -3.00 D.
 
• Adding the powers: 4.50 D + (-3.00 D) = 1.50 D.
 
• Thus, the combined power of the lenses is +1.5 D.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lens Power**

 
 
• The power of a lens (measured in diopters, D) is the reciprocal of its focal length in meters (P = 1/f).
 
• Converging lenses have positive powers, while diverging lenses have negative powers.
 
 
 
• **Types of Lenses**
 
 
• Convex lenses (converging lenses) focus parallel rays of light to a single point.
 
• Concave lenses (diverging lenses) spread out parallel rays of light.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Lenses**
 
 
• Convex lenses are used in magnifying glasses, cameras, and eyeglasses for hyperopia (farsightedness).
 
• Concave lenses are used in eyeglasses for myopia (nearsightedness) and in certain types of cameras and telescopes.
 
 
 
• **Combination of Lenses**
 
 
• When multiple lenses are combined, their overall power is the sum of their individual powers.
 
• This principle is used in designing complex optical systems like microscopes and telescopes.

The correct answer is __**Ovary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The ovary is a part of the female reproductive organ in flowering plants (angiosperms).
 
• It contains ovules, which after fertilization develop into seeds.
 
• As the ovules mature into seeds, the ovary walls thicken and develop into the fruit.
 
• This transformation process ensures the protection and dispersion of seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flower Structure**

 
 
• The flower is the reproductive structure of angiosperms, consisting of male (stamens) and female (carpels) parts.
 
• The stamen includes the anther and filament, while the carpel comprises the stigma, style, and ovary.
 
 
 
• **Pollination and Fertilization**
 
 
• Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of a flower.
 
• Fertilization occurs when the pollen tube delivers sperm cells to the ovule, leading to the formation of seeds.
 
 
 
• **Fruit Formation**
 
 
• Post fertilization, the ovary undergoes changes and develops into a fruit.
 
• Fruits protect the enclosed seeds and assist in their dispersal to new locations.
 
 
 
• **Types of Fruits**
 
 
• Simple fruits develop from a single ovary, while aggregate fruits come from multiple ovaries of one flower.
 
• Multiple fruits are formed from the ovaries of multiple flowers growing in a cluster.

questions.question: Amita bought a laptop at a 20% discount on its marked price. If she paid ₹28,400 for the laptop, what was its marked price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Marked Price (MP)** be 100%.

Given **Discount** = 20%, therefore **Selling Price (SP)** = 100% − 20% = 80%.

According to the question, 80% = ₹28,400.

Ratio-unitary method: 100% = (28,400 ÷ 80) × 100.

100% = 355 × 100 = ₹35,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹35,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹28,400 and **Discount%** = 20%.

**Formula:** SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d5222dfb81be9f119068a1ae10b8239890637df1e5853cd85ca7daa6cfe1c3c.png] 

⇒ 28,400 = MP × (100 − 20) ÷ 100

⇒ 28,400 = MP × 80 ÷ 100

⇒ 28,400 = MP × 4 ÷ 5

⇒ MP = (28,400 × 5) ÷ 4

⇒ MP = 7,100 × 5 = 35,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹35,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

**Marked Price (MP)** is the price printed on an item. The **Selling Price (SP)** is obtained by subtracting the discount from the MP. Formula: Discount = MP − SP.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts a% and b% are given, the single equivalent discount is calculated as (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.
